newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Nov 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Nov 5.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Czech National Bank's proposal for the privatisation of the big four Czech banks apparently did not get Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's approval. One area which is evidently controversial is the proposed fusion of CSOB and Ceska Sporitelna.

- The Ministry of Trade and Industry is considering proposing a legislative amendment which will allow state-owned Transgas, the de facto monopoly for natural gas importing, an exclusive import licence according to Minister Vladimir Dlouhy.

- After implementing cost-saving plans, the state once again was in the black in October. State receipts totalled 394 billion crowns while expenditures totalled 392.8 billion crowns for a surplus of 1.2 billion crowns.

- Because of The Czech Republic's size, geographic location, raw materials and economic structure, the country cannot manage to post long-term trade surpluses, according to Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus.

- Ceska Rafinerska a.s. has decreased the price of petrol by 100 crowns a tonne and diesel fuel by 150 crowns a tonne. The company, the Czech Republic's largest fuel producer, has implemented plans to adjust fuel prices weekly to correspond to price fluctuations in the world market.
- Construction is one of the fastest developing branches of the Czech economy, but the least debt-ridden according to the Czech Statistical Bureau.
- Neither devaluation nor implementing import tariffs are currently a solution to the problem of the trade imbalance, according to the Ministry of Trade and Industry.

- Banks are revising their attitude towards leasing companies and are lending money to them again. In the first half of this year banks refused to provide any finances to leasing companies, considering them to be high-risk.

- Esso Praha sro, owned by America's Exxon Corp, is not intending to obtain more than five percent of the filling station market. The market here is saturated, according to a representative from the firm.
- Zbrojovska Brno a.s., a manufacturer of hunting and sports rifles, wants to extend its production to include pistols.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The first elections to Senate, later this month are likely to be a battle between the Civic Democratic Party and the Social Democrats, according to recent polls. Independant candidates have little chance of winning a seat.
- Water prices are expected to rise next year by nine to 15 percent.
- The Czech crown, which fluctuated before the parliamentary elections earlier this year, has remained stable in the run up to the senatorial elections.
